intro.title: FUNDA — Live Search Bar
intro.body: In this lesson you will build a Live Search Bar component that queries a REST API as the user types, debouncing keystrokes to avoid flooding the network and automatically cancelling stale requests when a newer query arrives. You will wire a text input to an Observable pipeline using RxJS operators, render results with the async pipe, and handle both loading and error states inline. The finished widget performs like the search bars in GitHub, Notion, or VS Code's command palette — responsive, efficient, and resilient to fast typing.
intro.usecase: Search-as-you-type is one of the most common UX patterns in modern web applications — used in e-commerce product search, admin user lookups, HR directory search, and code editors. Getting it right means understanding request cancellation, debounce timing, and graceful degradation when the API is slow. These are the exact patterns you will be asked about in senior Angular interviews when they ask "how does your search component handle race conditions?"
